notesDetails.title: Full 7/7 Spec & Holdout Pass (61/61 Tests, 0 Credo Issues) on OpenCode's Free Inkling 2 Small Tier
bullets: Complete Outside-In Delivery Across 10 Commits: Over 1h 45m 58s (07:44:57–09:30:55 WIB in `20261111T004457Z.events.jsonl`, preceded by a 1.4s `provider.no-route` failure at 07:44:40 when `run_opencode.fish` was initially invoked on default `openai/gpt-6-sol`), `opencode/inkling-2-small-free#high` (Thinking Machines Lab's 17B-active / 594B-total MoE model) completed all 7 stages (`S1`–`S7`) plus release verification in 10 commits (`2a36b6b` → `2f73c81`).

All Verification Gates Green: `mix format --check-formatted` passed cleanly, `mix credo` reported 0 issues across 24 files (`146 mods/funs`), and `mix test` passed 61/61 tests in 87.1s (`66.8s async, 20.2s sync`).

Strict Git Hygiene Recovery (Steps 82–83): When committing S1 at Step 82 (`git add -A`), the agent noticed `records/20261111T004440Z.*` and `records/20261111T004457Z.*` had been staged into `2a36b6b`. On the very next step (Step 83), it ran `git rm -q --cached records/... && git commit --amend --no-edit -q` and used explicit paths or `':!records'` for the remaining 9 commits.

notesDetails.title: Empirically Audited & Rejected Erlang :httpc After Proving 3xx/4xx/5xx Bodies Are Buffered Whole
bullets: 24-Step Empirical `:httpc` Investigation (Steps 98–121, 5m 20s): At the start of S3, the agent built disposable probes under `/tmp/opencode/httpc_exp` testing `:httpc.request/5` with `stream: :self` and `{:sync, false}` against local servers returning `200`, `302`, `404`, and `503`.

Pinpointing `IS_STREAMED` in OTP `inets` Source (Steps 114–121): While `200 OK` produced `{:http, {ref, :stream_start, headers}}` chunks, `302`/`404`/`503` returned a single buffered `{{vsn, status, phrase}, headers, body}` tuple. Inspecting `/nix/store/.../inets/src/http_client/httpc_handler.erl` at Steps 118–121 confirmed `:httpc` only streams `200` and `206` responses, violating the V1 contract requirement to stream and discard response bodies for every status.

Zero-Dependency `CapyBench.Connection` Over `:gen_tcp` & `:ssl`: The agent implemented a custom HTTP/1.1 client with an absolute monotonic deadline (`System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) + timeout_ms`), 64 KiB response-head / 8 KiB line caps, 64 KiB chunked/Content-Length/EOF body discard, keep-alive socket reuse without automatic retries, and `:ssl` peer verification (`verify: :verify_peer`, `:public_key.cacerts_get/0` + `CB_EXTRA_CA_CERT` DER injection, and `:public_key.pkix_verify_hostname_match_fun(:https)`).

notesDetails.title: Four Real Signal & PTY Fixes in S1/S7: +Bi SIGUSR1 Wrapper, POSIX Trap Wait Loop & OTP Boot Handler
bullets: 1. Bypassing the BEAM Break Handler (`./cb` + `+Bi`, Steps 7–68): Probing `:os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle)` at Step 9 raised `ArgumentError` because the BEAM reserves `SIGINT` for its break handler, and plain escripts exited 0 on Ctrl-C without running Elixir code. After inspecting OTP's `erl_signal_server.erl` in `/nix/store` (Steps 38–43), the agent configured `escript: [main_module: CapyBench.CLI, name: "cb-escript", emu_args: "+Bi"]`, added a committed POSIX `./cb` wrapper that traps `INT`/`TERM` and forwards `kill -USR1 "$child"`, and installed `CapyBench.SignalHandler` on `:erl_signal_server`.

2. Moving Signal Registration to `CapyBench.Application.start/2` (Steps 320–337): During S7 `expect` PTY testing, early Ctrl-C signals crashed the BEAM with `"Received SIGUSR1\nCrash dump is being written..."` on stderr because `SIGUSR1` arrived while the VM was still booting before `CapyBench.CLI.main/1` ran. Creating `CapyBench.Application` to install `CapyBench.SignalHandler` at OTP application startup eliminated the boot race.

3. Fixing POSIX `sh` Interrupted `wait` SIGHUP Race (Steps 338–347): Even with the boot handler installed, `expect` PTY runs produced empty stdout because in POSIX `/bin/sh`, `wait "$child"` returns immediately (status > 128) as soon as the `trap` handler fires while `cb-escript` is still finishing its in-flight request; `./cb` then exited, closing the PTY master and SIGHUP-killing the BEAM before `CapyBench.Summary` could print. Looping `while kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; do wait "$child"; rc=$?; done` kept the PTY open until `cb-escript` settled.

4. Eliminating Pacing Sleep-Slicing Throughput Regression (Steps 350–357): Slicing all pacing sleeps into 10ms polling chunks caused OS timer overhead that dropped 5s loop throughput from 50 to 38–39 requests (~24% loss), breaking 3 `HTTPTest` assertions. Restricting `sleep_with_interrupt_check/2` slicing to waits `> 500ms` (the post-50-cap window drain) restored 50/50 throughput while keeping Ctrl-C responsive.

notesDetails.title: Caught & Fixed Two Subtle Contract Deviations in S6/Release Verification (4.9s Early Exit & TLS Logger on stdout)
bullets: 50-Start Cap Early Return at ~4.90s (Steps 262–265): While testing S6 against a local server, the agent noticed that when all 50 requests completed rapidly on a reused keep-alive connection (the 50th request dispatching at ~4.90s), the loop exited immediately at `Elapsed: 4.91 s` instead of waiting for the 5.00s start window to close. It updated `CapyBench.Benchmark` (`acc.started >= @max_starts`) to drain the remaining start window (`max(acc.deadline - current, 0)`) and added a deterministic test asserting `summary.elapsed_ms >= 5_000`.

OTP `:logger` Writing TLS `:notice` Alerts to `stdout` (Steps 373–382, `32c0acd`): During post-S7 release verification against an untrusted HTTPS server, byte-count checks (`stdout=$(wc -c < t_out.txt)B`) revealed OTP's `:ssl` handshake logged `[notice] TLS :client: ... Unknown CA` to `stdout`, violating the contract that diagnostics go to `stderr`. When `:logger.update_handler_config(:default, :config, %{type: :standard_error})` failed at Step 377 because `:logger_std_h` forbids mutating `:type` in place, the agent removed and re-added `:default` with `type: :standard_error` in `CapyBench.Application.start/2`.

notesDetails.title: 390 Strict Single-Tool Turns Across a 378.4k Uncompacted Context Window (99.45% Cache Hit Rate)
bullets: Zero Parallel Tool Calls (389 Tool Calls in 390 Steps): Across the entire 106-minute session, `inkling-2-small-free` never batched multiple tool calls in a single turn—executing exactly 1 tool call in Steps 1–389 (`261 shell`, `76 edit`, `39 write`, `13 read`) and finishing with a text summary in Step 390.

99.45% Prefix Cache Hit Rate with Zero Compactions: Prompt context grew monotonically from `1,929` tokens (Step 1) to `378,440` tokens (Step 390; `36.09%` of its `1,048,576` context window) with zero cache evictions or compactions, serving `72,730,624` cached tokens against `403,232` uncached input tokens and `317,617` output tokens (`207,734` reasoning + `109,883` visible/tool output; `73,451,473` total tokens).

Three 120s Shell Timeouts & Seven `edit` Mismatches: All 7 tool errors were `edit` `oldString` mismatches (`2` duplicate matches, `5` whitespace/context misses) that were immediately resolved on the next turn. In `shell`, 3 commands hit 120s timeouts: two during S1 signal probing (Step 25 `ctrlc2` `+Bd` loop and Step 31 `find /nix/store -name "os.xml"`) and one at Step 218 when running the full `mix test` suite with a 120s timeout after S4 added multiple 5s-loop CLI tests.
